senses.gloss: (b. h.; עפר to be thick, dust, mud, sand, mortar.
units: Gen. R. s. 14 (ref. to Gen. II, 7) ע׳ זכר אדמה נקבה היוצר מביא ע׳ זכר וכ׳ ‘afar represents the male element, ădamah, the female; the potter takes male dust (coarse sand) and female earth (soft clay), in order that the vessels be strong.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 2:2">Sot. II, 2</cite> <he>נוטל ע׳ מתחתיה</he> he (the priest) takes earth from under it (the marble slab).

Ib. 16ᵃ מצינו אפר שקרוי ע׳ we find that ashes are likewise called ‘afar; Ḥull. 88ᵇ; Gen. R. s. 49ᵇ. Ib. עֲפַר סוטה the dust used in preparing the Water of Jealousy; עֲ׳ כיסוי the earth or ashes used for covering up the blood at slaughtering (Lev. XVII, 13); Num. R. s. 9.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 9:50">Ib.</cite> <he>זכתה … ואנכי ע׳ ואפר לא זכתה תחזור לעַפְרָהּ</he> if she is worthy (innocent), let a son descend from her like Abraham, of whom it is written, ‘And I am dust and ashes’ (<cite ref="Genesis 18:27">Gen. XVIII, 27</cite>); if she is unworthy, let her return to her native dust.
<cite ref="Genesis 18:27">Ib.</cite> <he>עֲ׳ זהב העגל</he> the gold dust of the calf. Y. B. Mets. VIII, end, 11ᵈ <he>ע׳ שחור</he> black potter’s earth; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 94:9">Gen. R. s. 94</cite> <he>עַפְרוֹ של יצחק</he> (ed. Wil. <he>אֶפְרוֹ</he>), v. <cite ref="A02793"><he>אֵפֶר</he></cite>.—Pl. <he>עֲפָרוֹת</he>, constr. <he>עַפְרוֹת</he>. Num. R. l. c. (ref. to <he>ומן העפר</he>, <cite ref="Numbers 5:17">Num. V, 17</cite>) [read:] <he>זהו ע׳ הזהב אשר טחן</he> this refers to the gold dust which he (Moses) made by grinding (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 9:21">Deut. IX, 21</cite>).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 26:7">Gen. R. s. 26</cite> <he>שהיו בקיאים בע׳ וכ׳</he> they were experts on the qualities of soil like serpents; a. e.
